newsitem.title: SPAIN: Madrid airport traffic is stabilising, AENA says.
newsitem.headline: Madrid airport traffic is stabilising, AENA says.

text.p: The number of aircraft movements at Madrid's Barajas airport rose only 3.5 percent in May to 21,920, implying traffic growth at the overcrowded airport has stabilised, the airports authority AENA said in a statement.

It also gave preliminary cargo totals for May which showed Barajas handled 21,817 tonnes of cargo last month, 10.5 percent more than May 1996. The five month total is now 11.4 percent ahead of the same period last year.
Barajas is full at peak times and a sudden increase in demand for slots at the end of last year led to serious delays affecting up to 50 percent of flights.
The slight increase in aircraft numbers in May indicates this growth in demand has slackened, AENA said.
"Anyway we do not expect noticeable increases in the future, given the saturation of flights during daytime hours," it added.

Passenger numbers were 6.8 percent higher in May at 1.95 million, bringing the increase in the first five months of the year to 10.8 percent. This shows airlines are filling a greater proportion of their seats, AENA said. - Reuters Air Cargo Service Tel+ 44 171 542 7706 Fax +5017 - www.racs.com
